title: Curious to hear what this community really thinks about my AI game
author: Winter-Atmosphere-95
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I have received so much negativity because I used AI for my game but so curious to hear input from people who actually dont hate AI lol

My dev partner and I are indie creators who normally stick to a standard Unity workflow. We kept seeing how much AI was evolving for game development and wanted to see what it could actually handle if we fully committed to testing it out.

It took a couple of months of trial and error, but we actually have a fully functioning game now. We just put our cozy hex-grid puzzle game, Hexcavate, up for sale on Steam. It's a relaxing logic puzzle about dwarves mining floating islands by turning tiles to route bombs into boulders.  

To get this done, we worked together using Claude to help write scripts and figure out the logic in Unity. For the visual side, we generated our base 2D game assets using ChatGPT, and then we took those into Photoshop to manually customize and clean everything up to fit the game's style.

It was definitely a learning curve trying to figure out how to fit everything together smoothly, but the workflow ended up working out really well for us.  
Here is the result if you want to check it out: [Hexcavate on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5239340/Hexcavate/)

**Thanks!!**

comments.author: Teh_Blue_Team
comments.body: Looks pretty, and unique. Will definitely check it out. Nice work!

comments.author: HuWeiliu
comments.body: Looks cool! Trailer is a little weird, hardly showed the game play at all outside of a few very quick moments. Mostly was just before and after states with the occasional unnecessary descriptions that Claude loves to pump out i.e." bombs wait for your turn". No one viewing the trailer was like "I really wanna know if the bombs I briefly saw there wait for my turn or not".
